objective: Build the missing mechanical robot-joint plant from motor shaft through ratio, reflected inertia, mission duty, precision error, compliance, resonance, encoders, output bearing, friction/backdrive and holding-brake handover; then reconstruct a current Harmonic Drive manufacturer catalog and Williamson's 1995 Series Elastic Actuators thesis as separate source-bound evidence spines.

request_interpretation.curriculum_intent: Insert the physical actuator between electromagnetic torque/STO and generic feedback control so the reader no longer treats a robot joint as an ideal torque multiplier.
request_interpretation.depth_intent: Write a private thirty-six-premise vertical-axis failure first and require the public bundle to provide enough insight to diagnose every premise without printing the problem as a quiz.
request_interpretation.source_intent: Separate transferable mechanics, current manufacturer selection evidence and a foundational primary-source reconstruction. Preserve artifact identity, author intent, page anchors, assumptions, admitted failures and prohibited transfer.
request_interpretation.formula_intent: Render every display equation with Korean operation annotations and one adjacent FormulaNote. Recompose long equations semantically when mobile scale falls rather than lowering the threshold or adding scroll.
request_interpretation.visual_intent: Use mechanism-specific observables: shaft boundary, ratio workbench, inertia bars, duty trace, hysteresis curve, compliance strip, resonance response, encoder residual, bearing load plane, torque-speed quadrant, brake timeline and change ledger.
request_interpretation.small_model_intent: Record atomic scope, source, premise, formula, Viz, critic, integration and QA-repair packets so 4B/9B models can replay bounded work without receiving the full curriculum in one prompt.

existing_coverage: robot-drive-isolation-emc-functional-safety separates STO, holding and motion-safe claims
robot-dynamics-feedback-control explains abstract state-space and feedback methods
missing_chain: a declared motor/output reference side for torque, speed, angle and inertia
ratio, efficiency and power accounting without free torque
pose-dependent reflected inertia and gravity/acceleration demand
peak, repeated peak, RMS, average speed and life on different clocks
backlash, lost motion, hysteresis, repeatability and transmission accuracy as different tests
series compliance, stored energy, structural stiffness and two-mass resonance
motor/output encoder observability and stiffness-calibrated torque estimation
radial, axial and offset-moment loads at the output bearing
holding-brake torque overlap, delay, wear and vertical-axis handover

scope_split.concept: Robot Actuator Mechanics owns transferable physical reasoning and system evidence.
scope_split.company_reference: Harmonic Drive Mechatronics 05/2026 preserves exact selection order, product-bound values, page identity and disclaimer.
scope_split.foundational_source: Williamson 1995 reconstructs author intent, minimal model, saturation analysis, hardware evidence, mismatch and admitted limitations.
scope_split.deferred: Gear-tooth design, final vendor life, brake certification, full manipulator flexible dynamics and controller tuning for an actual robot remain exact-system work.

private_transfer_gate.scenario: A gravity-loaded seven-axis shoulder uses a 3 N·m motor, 100:1 strain-wave reducer, one motor encoder, integrated output bearing and motor brake. The team calls it a 300 N·m zero-error joint, sizes from one peak and a universal 5:1 inertia heuristic, copies catalog values across ratio/revision, ignores housing and two-mass modes, observes only motor angle, omits bearing moment and uses the holding brake for every stop while commanding STO before engagement.

coverage_groups.public_resolution: Actuator boundary and ratio/power section; Joint Labs 01-02; motor/output side and efficiency notes.
Reflected inertia section and Lab 03; base inertia ledger, pose-dependent load and signed torque demand.
Mission duty section and Lab 04; peak/repeated/RMS/average-speed clocks and life boundary.
Accuracy section and Lab 05; stimulus-specific curve states and catalog non-transfer ledger.
Compliance section and Lab 06; piecewise stiffness, stored energy and series structural compliance.
Two-mass section and Lab 07; full relative mode versus manufacturer one-inertia shortcut and bandwidth warning.
Dual-encoder section and Lab 08; link angle, deformation, torque estimate and calibration/synchronization failure.
Output-bearing section and Lab 09; force offset, moment, dynamic L10 and static/shock boundary.
Friction/backdrive section, Lab 10 and Williamson force/impedance trade.
Brake handover section and Lab 11; operational stop, hold, STO, startup/shutdown sequence and wear state.
Joint commissioning Lab 12 and evidence-intersection equation invalidate dependent rows after change.

private_transfer_gate.publication_policy: The compound scenario remains private. Public prose, formulas, interactions, counterexamples and source boundaries contain the transferable insight needed to solve it.

source_decisions.source: Harmonic Drive AG, Harmonic Drive Mechatronics
source_decisions.boundary: All numeric values, factors, examples and recommendations remain tied to exact product, size, ratio, mounting, lubrication, test condition and revision. Averages are not silently converted to guaranteed minima.

source_decisions.source: Matthew M. Williamson, Series Elastic Actuators
source_decisions.identity: MIT AI Technical Report 1524 / M.S. thesis, January 1995, 83 PDF pages
source_decisions.boundary: The ideal clamped linear model is not projected over stiction, backlash, electronics, saturation, moving environments, modern controllers or full robot safety.

source_decisions.source: Kollmorgen Application Sizing and Holding Brake guidance
source_decisions.boundary: The drive brake-control function is not personal-safety proof; no fixed inertia ratio is treated as a universal stability theorem.

source_decisions.source: SKF Rolling Bearings catalog and ISO 281 workflow
used_for: equivalent dynamic and static load distinction
source_decisions.boundary: Basic L10 does not guarantee service life under unmodeled shock, contamination, lubrication, mounting, preload, misalignment, seals or housing behavior.

source_decisions.source: M. W. Spong, Modeling and Control of Elastic Joint Robots, 1987
used_for: historical bridge from rigid to elastic-joint modeling
source_decisions.boundary: No detailed equation reconstruction was attributed because the full primary text was not locally auditable in this run.

source_extraction.tooling: pypdf/pdfplumber text inspection plus pypdfium2 rendered-page review; Poppler was unavailable and no privileged package installation was used.

events.observed: The curriculum could produce and remove motor torque but generic feedback control assumed an unexplained plant and actuator input.
events.inference: Readers could tune a rigid ideal joint while missing ratio-side errors, compliance, bearing and brake mechanics.
events.decision: Insert a mechanical actuator foundation before controller implementation and bind it to FOC, braking, STO and feedback paths.
events.verification: The concept article supplies twelve causal sections and the learning graph links all five boundaries.

events.observed: A joint can satisfy ideal torque multiplication while thirty-six duty, precision, dynamic, sensing, bearing and holding premises remain false.
events.inference: A catalog summary would not force implementation-level understanding.
events.decision: Use the private thirty-six-premise vertical-axis scenario as the pre-authoring coverage gate.
events.verification: Every premise is mapped to public prose, equation, observable, source boundary or change-evidence gate.

events.observed: Manufacturer catalog rules and a foundational research thesis answer different questions and carry different evidence types.
events.inference: Mixing them into one concept article would make current product recommendations look universal and ideal theory look like a catalog guarantee.
events.decision: Create separate Harmonic Drive company-reference and Williamson foundational-source articles around one transferable concept spine.
events.verification: The catalog has seven page-bound states; the thesis follows intent, model, saturation, identification, contact and admitted-limit evidence.

events.observed: A repeated box-arrow pipeline could not make duty, hysteresis, resonance, bearing geometry and brake overlap visible.
events.inference: Color changes would not produce a better mental model.
events.decision: Match each concept to a different observable geometry and require state changes to alter a conclusion.
events.verification: All twelve labs changed causal state; mobile and desktop screenshots showed chart, control, legend and status without clipping or inner scroll.

events.observed: The first browser run measured concept/catalog minimum formula scales of 0.52/0.67 at 360 px and 0.56/0.73 at 390 px.
events.inference: The formulas technically fit but the long one-line evidence intersection, inertia ledger and resonance assumption were not comfortably readable.
events.decision: Split the inertia ledger into base and reflected stages, the evidence intersection into two semantic groups, and resonance into equation and assumption lines. Rewrite piecewise stiffness with per-region delta variables.
events.verification: Public post-font-load minimum scales became concept/catalog/paper 0.84/0.89/0.85 at 360 px and 0.89/0.94/0.94 at 390 px.

events.decision: Keep internal lab index in the accessible label and show only the global V number plus JOINT LAB role on screen.
events.verification: The caption no longer presents a second visible numeric sequence.

next_milestone.title: Robot Structural Mechanics, Materials, Fatigue & Thermal Design
next_milestone.reason: The actuator article closes torque transmission inside one joint but still treats housing, link, fasteners, material, fatigue and thermal expansion as lumped stiffness or assumptions.
next_milestone.planned_boundary: Free-body diagrams and load paths, stress/strain and safety factors, beam torsion/bending, stiffness versus strength, stress concentration, fasteners and joints, fatigue/S-N and load spectra, modal/FEA evidence, thermal expansion and tolerance stack, and physical test correlation. It will not issue a final structure rating without geometry, material lot, process, load spectrum and failure criterion.
